scenes.visual: Title card 'Two Copies, One Coin Toss' fades in over a single open pea pod. THE WORLD, kept for both chapters (16:9, warm cream background). COLOUR MAP, same in every scene: round copy / round seeds GOLD; wrinkled copy / wrinkled seeds BROWN; yellow copy BRIGHT YELLOW; green copy GREEN; gametes are small white circles (egg) or small white grains (pollen); coin is SILVER. Allele letters (R, r, Y, y) and every number appear only as on-screen text, never spoken. Seeds are simple cartoons, not photographs; anything not computed is labelled 'schematic'.

scenes.tts: Where can a trait hide for a whole generation? Mendel asked that of garden peas.
scenes.visual: Two pea plants side by side, labelled 'true-breeding round' (GOLD seeds) and 'true-breeding wrinkled' (BROWN seeds). Under each, a small loop arrow labelled 'selfed: same form every generation'.
scenes.narration: Where can a trait hide for a whole generation? Mendel asked that of garden peas.

scenes.tts: He started with lines that always bred true. One line always gave round seeds. The other always gave wrinkled seeds.
scenes.visual: Three generations of each line stack downward, each row showing identical seeds: all GOLD round on the left, all BROWN wrinkled on the right.
scenes.narration: He started with lines that always bred true. One line always gave round seeds. The other always gave wrinkled seeds.

scenes.tts: Then he crossed them by hand. He opened a young flower, removed its stamens, which make pollen, and brushed on pollen from the other line.
scenes.visual: Close-up schematic of a pea flower: tweezers lift away the stamens; a brush carries GOLD-tagged pollen from the round plant to the stigma of the wrinkled plant. Label 'cross by hand'.
scenes.narration: Then he crossed them by hand. He opened a young flower, removed its stamens, which make pollen, and brushed on pollen from the other line.

scenes.tts: Every hybrid seed was round, like the round parent. Not halfway between. Wrinkled seemed to be gone.
scenes.visual: A pod opens to show a row of identical GOLD round seeds, labelled 'hybrid seeds (F1)'. A faint BROWN outline of a wrinkled seed fades out beside them with a question mark.
scenes.narration: Every hybrid seed was round, like the round parent. Not halfway between. Wrinkled seemed to be gone.

scenes.tts: He planted those round hybrid seeds and let each plant pollinate itself. Their pods held round and wrinkled peas, side by side. Wrinkled was back, unchanged.
scenes.visual: The F1 seed grows into a plant (label 'F1 plant'). Its pod opens: GOLD round and BROWN wrinkled peas side by side in one pod, labelled 'F2 seeds, scored in the F1 plant's pods'.
scenes.narration: He planted those round hybrid seeds and let each plant pollinate itself. Their pods held round and wrinkled peas, side by side. Wrinkled was back, unchanged.

scenes.tts: He counted thousands of these seeds. Round beat wrinkled by about three to one. So where was wrinkled hiding, and why one in four?
scenes.caption: He counted thousands of these seeds. Round beat wrinkled by about 3 to 1. So where was wrinkled hiding, and why one in four?
scenes.visual: Two bars grow: GOLD bar '5,474 round', BROWN bar '1,850 wrinkled'. Text appears: '2.96 : 1'. A question mark hovers over the BROWN bar.
scenes.narration: He counted thousands of these seeds. Round beat wrinkled by about 3 to 1. So where was wrinkled hiding, and why one in four?

scenes.tts: Here is the answer in modern terms. Each pea plant carries two copies of the gene for seed shape. One copy came from each parent.
scenes.visual: A pea plant outline with two cards inside it. Arrows show one card arriving from a mother plant and one from a father plant. Label 'two copies of the seed-shape gene'.
scenes.narration: Here is the answer in modern terms. Each pea plant carries two copies of the gene for seed shape. One copy came from each parent.

scenes.tts: Picture the copies as cards. A round line holds two round cards. A wrinkled line holds two wrinkled cards. The hybrid holds one of each.
scenes.visual: Three plants in a row, each with two cards: GOLD+GOLD labelled 'RR', BROWN+BROWN labelled 'rr', GOLD+BROWN labelled 'Rr, hybrid'. The hybrid's pair glows.
scenes.narration: Picture the copies as cards. A round line holds two round cards. A wrinkled line holds two wrinkled cards. The hybrid holds one of each.

scenes.tts: When the hybrid makes an egg or a pollen grain, it puts in just one card. Which card is decided like a fair coin toss.
scenes.visual: A SILVER coin flips above a white egg circle: heads, the GOLD card drops into it; tails, the BROWN card does. The same flip then plays above a pollen grain. Repeat four or five times quickly, building an egg tray and a pollen tray that each hold both kinds.
scenes.narration: When the hybrid makes an egg or a pollen grain, it puts in just one card. Which card is decided like a fair coin toss.

scenes.tts: So half its eggs carry a round copy, and half carry a wrinkled copy. The same is true of its pollen.
scenes.visual: Two trays: 'eggs' and 'pollen'. Each fills to exactly half GOLD, half BROWN gametes. Text '1/2 R, 1/2 r' under each tray.
scenes.narration: So half its eggs carry a round copy, and half carry a wrinkled copy. The same is true of its pollen.

scenes.tts: Now the hybrid pollinates itself. Eggs meet pollen at random, so four unions are equally likely. One box gets two round copies. Two get one of each. One gets two wrinkled copies.
scenes.visual: A two-by-two grid builds: eggs down the side (R, r), pollen across the top (R, r). Each box fills as an egg and pollen grain slide together: GOLD+GOLD, GOLD+BROWN, BROWN+GOLD, BROWN+BROWN. Genotype text appears in each box: RR, Rr, Rr, rr, and below the grid '1 : 2 : 1'.
scenes.narration: Now the hybrid pollinates itself. Eggs meet pollen at random, so four unions are equally likely. One box gets two round copies. Two get one of each. One gets two wrinkled copies.

scenes.tts: Remember, every hybrid seed was round, with one copy of each. So which of these four boxes will look round?
scenes.visual: The grid holds. Each box shows only its two cards, no seed yet. A question card: 'Which boxes look round?'
scenes.narration: Remember, every hybrid seed was round, with one copy of each. So which of these four boxes will look round?

scenes.visual: Predict pause. Grid and question card hold. A 5-second ring timer at bottom right.

scenes.tts: Three of them. One round copy is enough for a round seed. Mendel called round the dominant form, the one the hybrid shows.
scenes.visual: Seeds appear in the boxes: GOLD round seeds in RR, Rr, Rr; a BROWN wrinkled seed in rr. Text: 'dominant: the form the hybrid shows'.
scenes.narration: Three of them. One round copy is enough for a round seed. Mendel called round the dominant form, the one the hybrid shows.

scenes.tts: Wrinkled is the recessive form. It hides in the hybrid, and shows only with two wrinkled copies.
scenes.visual: The rr box glows. Text: 'recessive: hidden in the hybrid, shows with two copies'. The Rr boxes briefly show a faint BROWN card behind each GOLD seed.
scenes.narration: Wrinkled is the recessive form. It hides in the hybrid, and shows only with two wrinkled copies.

scenes.tts: So the hidden mix is one, two, one. What you see is three round to one wrinkled.
scenes.caption: So the hidden mix is 1 : 2 : 1. What you see is 3 round to 1 wrinkled.
scenes.visual: Two labels under the grid: 'genotypes 1 RR : 2 Rr : 1 rr' and 'phenotypes 3 round : 1 wrinkled', with brackets grouping the three GOLD boxes.
scenes.narration: So the hidden mix is 1 : 2 : 1. What you see is 3 round to 1 wrinkled.

scenes.tts: Back to Mendel's count. It came close to three to one, but not exactly. Real counts scatter around what the coin toss predicts.
scenes.caption: Back to Mendel's count. It came close to 3 to 1, but not exactly. Real counts scatter around what the coin toss predicts.
scenes.visual: The two bars from s06 return. A WHITE dashed line marks the expected 3:1 split (5,493 : 1,831 for 7,324 seeds, computed). The GOLD bar ends just below its line, the BROWN just above. Text: 'expected 3 : 1, counted 2.96 : 1'.
scenes.narration: Back to Mendel's count. It came close to 3 to 1, but not exactly. Real counts scatter around what the coin toss predicts.

scenes.tts: So here is the idea. Every pea plant has two copies. Every egg and pollen grain gets one, by a coin toss. One round copy is enough to look round.
scenes.visual: The plant with two cards, the coin, and the gamete tray line up left to right. The three sentences appear one at a time beside them.
scenes.narration: So here is the idea. Every pea plant has two copies. Every egg and pollen grain gets one, by a coin toss. One round copy is enough to look round.

scenes.tts: If that is right, the round seeds are not all the same. Some hide a wrinkled copy. How could you find out which?
scenes.visual: Three GOLD round seeds in a row. Behind two of them a faint BROWN card shimmers; behind one, nothing. A question mark sits over the row.
scenes.narration: If that is right, the round seeds are not all the same. Some hide a wrinkled copy. How could you find out which?

scenes.visual: End card, large text centred: 'Pea plants carry two copies; each gamete gets one, by coin toss.'
